program.merge_policy: accumulate twenty 25-finding deep passes; consolidate, source-revalidate, and run heavy repository validation after Wave 2500

source_provenance: Direct PubMed/NCBI discovery and abstract/source verification
PMID-level dedupe against cumulative Wave 2000 index

waves.title: The Effectiveness of Melatonin for Sleep Disturbances in Parkinson' Disease: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
waves.population: 409 people with Parkinson disease across 8 studies
waves.finding: Melatonin improved subjective sleep quality, daytime sleepiness, sleep-onset latency, and total sleep time, but subjective improvements did not reach the minimal clinically important difference and objective sleep outcomes were not consistently improved.
waves.safety: Reported as well tolerated in the review; Parkinson-disease findings should not be generalized to healthy adults.

waves.title: Association Between Levels of Magnesium and Diabetic Retinopathy in Diabetic Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
waves.population: 2,232 people with type 2 diabetes across 17 studies
waves.finding: Magnesium levels were lower in people with diabetic retinopathy than diabetic controls without retinopathy, and lower still in proliferative versus non-proliferative disease; certainty was rated low and heterogeneity was very high.
waves.safety: Association does not establish that magnesium supplementation prevents or treats retinopathy.

waves.title: Efficacy and safety of perioperative magnesium on postoperative pain in adult patients undergoing cardiothoracic surgeries- a systematic review and meta-analysis.
waves.population: 1,140 adults undergoing cardiothoracic surgery
waves.finding: Perioperative magnesium modestly reduced 24-hour pain versus placebo, but the effect did not reach a minimal clinically important difference and did not improve opioid use, rescue analgesia timing, or length of stay.
waves.safety: No major adverse events were reported, but dosing and perioperative routes were heterogeneous.

waves.title: Impacts of Milk Protein Supplementation on Lipid Profile, Blood Pressure, Oxidative Stress, and Liver Enzymes: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
waves.population: adults receiving casein, whey, or other milk-protein supplementation
waves.finding: Milk-protein supplementation produced small reductions in total cholesterol, systolic blood pressure, and triglycerides, with no significant pooled effects on LDL-C, HDL-C, diastolic pressure, several oxidative-stress markers, or liver enzymes.
waves.safety: Effects pool multiple milk-protein formulations and should not be assigned to a single product or dose.

waves.title: Effect of Protein Supplementation on Health-Related Quality of Life in Individuals With Advanced Chronic Kidney Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
waves.population: people with advanced chronic kidney disease, including dialysis
waves.finding: Protein/amino-acid supplementation did not clearly improve health-related quality of life; pooled analyses showed small increases in serum albumin and BMI.
waves.safety: Evidence was limited by few HRQOL studies, high risk of bias, and substantial heterogeneity; advanced CKD requires condition-specific nutrition management.

waves.title: The effectiveness of intervention with omega-3 fatty acids, eicosapentaenoic and docosahexenoic acid in peripheral arterial disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
waves.population: 759 people with peripheral arterial disease across 12 studies
waves.finding: EPA or EPA+DHA supplementation did not improve pain-free walking distance, maximal walking distance, ankle-brachial index, flow-mediated dilation, inflammatory markers, cholesterol, or blood pressure versus placebo.
waves.safety: The review could not rule out benefits of specific formulations or higher-dose EPA; the null applies to the studied PAD regimens.

waves.title: Caffeine and IBD Risk: A Meta-Analysis.
waves.study: meta-analysis of prospective, cross-sectional, and case-control studies
waves.population: 13,209 participants across 21 studies
waves.finding: Overall caffeine intake was not significantly associated with IBD risk, while subgroup signals varied substantially by region, age, caffeine source, smoking, and education.
waves.safety: Observational subgroup findings are vulnerable to confounding and should not be converted into causal intake advice.

waves.title: Effectiveness of alpha lipoic acid supplementation on biochemical, clinical, and inflammatory parameters in patients with diabetic polyneuropathy: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
waves.population: people with diabetic polyneuropathy across 15 included studies
waves.finding: Alpha-lipoic acid improved multiple neuropathic symptom outcomes, including paresthesia, numbness, and pain measures, while HbA1c and selected nerve-conduction outcomes were not significantly improved.
waves.safety: The review describes ALA as a potentially safe adjunct, but dose-specific superiority and long-term disease modification remain uncertain.

waves.title: Can probiotics reduce chemotherapy-induced complications in leukemia patients? A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
waves.population: 753 people with leukemia receiving chemotherapy
waves.finding: Probiotic interventions reduced several gastrointestinal chemotherapy complications in pooled analyses, including nausea, diarrhea, bloating, vomiting, and indigestion; constipation reporting was less convincing despite the authors' overall positive interpretation.
waves.safety: Strain composition and immunocompromised oncology populations require formulation- and population-specific safety interpretation.

waves.title: Efficacy and safety of probiotic/synbiotic supplementation for overweight or obese children: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
waves.population: 763 children with overweight or obesity
waves.finding: Probiotic/synbiotic supplementation modestly improved BMI-z and inflammatory markers CRP and TNF-alpha; benefits varied by age, duration, complications, and intervention type and disappeared in the NAFLD subgroup.
waves.safety: Pediatric and strain-specific evidence should not be generalized to adults or all probiotic products.

waves.title: Evaluating the efficacy of probiotics in schizophrenia and depression: A meta-analysis of clinical outcomes and subgroup effects.
waves.population: 893 participants with schizophrenia or depression
waves.finding: The review found no consistent evidence that probiotics improve depression or schizophrenia overall; heterogeneous subgroup signals were insufficient to establish reliable benefit.
waves.safety: Strain, population, geography, and co-supplementation differences limit generalization.

waves.title: The effect of dietary nitrate on weight management: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
waves.population: 199 adults with obesity
waves.finding: Dietary nitrate did not significantly reduce body weight or BMI, but pooled analyses suggested modest reductions in systolic blood pressure, total cholesterol, and triglycerides.
waves.safety: The evidence base was small and publication bias was detected for some outcomes; no weight-loss claim is supported.

waves.title: The beneficial effects of Chlorella vulgaris supplementation on health-related indices in patients with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease: a GRADE-assessed systematic review and meta-analysis.
waves.population: 375 people with NAFLD; all included studies conducted in Iran
waves.finding: Chlorella supplementation was associated with improvements in weight, fasting glucose, hs-CRP, LDL-C, total cholesterol, ALP, and AST.
waves.safety: GRADE certainty was very low and geographic concentration limits generalizability; results should remain provisional.

waves.title: A meta-analysis of the literature evaluating the impact of vitamin D on female fertility and ovarian reserve function.
waves.population: 2,111 women across 22 studies
waves.finding: Vitamin D supplementation was associated with improved dominant-follicle count, ovulation rate, and pregnancy rate, while AMH was not significantly changed.
waves.safety: The synthesis mixed vitamin-D status and supplementation studies, so causal supplementation claims require calibration to intervention-only evidence.

waves.title: Copper, Ceruloplasmin, Zinc, and Manganese Levels in Brain and Biological Fluids from Parkinson's Disease Patients: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
waves.population: people with Parkinson disease compared with controls
waves.finding: Parkinson disease was associated with altered copper, ceruloplasmin, zinc, and manganese concentrations across different tissues and fluids, with direction varying by specimen type.
waves.safety: Biomarker differences do not establish benefit from zinc, copper, or manganese supplementation and may reflect disease biology or confounding.

waves.title: Low Dose Versus High Dose Vitamin D for Treatment of Nutritional Rickets: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
waves.study: systematic review/meta-analysis of 4 randomized or quasi-randomized trials
waves.population: children with nutritional rickets
waves.finding: Low-dose and high-dose vitamin D regimens produced no statistically or clinically meaningful differences in 25(OH)D, radiologic improvement, PTH, or alkaline phosphatase at 12 weeks.
waves.safety: No serious clinical adverse events were reported; this is treatment of diagnosed pediatric rickets, not general supplementation guidance.

waves.title: Folic acid supplementation and malaria susceptibility and severity among people taking antifolate antimalarial drugs in endemic areas.
waves.study: Cochrane systematic review/meta-analysis of 8 randomized trials
waves.population: 3,486 people taking antifolate antimalarial drugs
waves.finding: Folic acid given with antifolate antimalarials reduced parasite clearance and increased treatment failure at several time points, especially in trials using doses above 1 mg/day.
waves.safety: Important drug-nutrient interaction signal; the 400-microgram trial showed little to no difference, so dose and antimalarial regimen matter.

waves.title: Therapeutic Effects of Dietary Supplements on Emotion-Related Symptoms in Children and Adolescents with Autism: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
waves.population: 866 children and adolescents with autism
waves.finding: Pooled dietary supplements modestly improved irritability and overall emotional symptoms but not anxiety; vitamin subgroups showed some irritability benefit while other supplement classes were nonsignificant.
waves.safety: High heterogeneity, mixed supplement classes, small samples, and risk-of-bias concerns prevent ingredient-specific conclusions.

waves.title: The effect of ginseng supplementation on CVD risk factors: a comprehensive systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis.
waves.population: 4,506 participants
waves.finding: Ginseng improved several inflammatory and oxidative-stress biomarkers but did not significantly improve anthropometric measures, blood pressure, glycemic profile, lipid profile, adipokines, or heart rate overall.
waves.safety: Dose-response signals were exploratory and should not be converted directly into consumer dosing recommendations.

waves.title: Lutein-fortified infant formula for newborn health: a comprehensive patent review and a systematic review of clinical trials.
waves.population: infants receiving lutein-fortified formula
waves.finding: Lutein-fortified formulas consistently increased circulating lutein versus unfortified formulas, but bioavailability remained lower than breast milk and evidence that fortification reproduces breast-milk-associated developmental effects was lacking.
waves.safety: Formula-specific infant evidence should not be generalized to standalone lutein supplements or adult eye-health products.

waves.title: The Safety and Efficacy of a Novel Saw Palmetto (Serenoa repens) Extract for Promoting Hair Growth in Adults With Self-Perceived Thinning Hair: 180-Day Results.
waves.population: 60 healthy adults with self-perceived thinning hair
waves.finding: A proprietary saw-palmetto fatty-acid extract increased terminal hair count, vellus hair count, and hair density versus placebo at 180 days.
waves.safety: No treatment-related adverse events were reported, but the sample was small and findings are specific to one proprietary extract.

waves.title: Is salivary melatonin an indicator of periodontal disease severity? A systematic review and meta-analysis.
waves.population: people with periodontal disease versus healthy controls
waves.finding: Salivary melatonin was substantially lower in periodontal disease, but heterogeneity was extreme and publication-bias signals were present.
waves.safety: This is biomarker association evidence, not evidence that melatonin supplementation treats periodontal disease.

waves.title: Effects of alpha-lipoic acid supplementation on patients with nonalcoholic fatty liver disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials.
waves.population: 414 people with NAFLD
waves.finding: Alpha-lipoic acid did not significantly improve liver enzymes, lipid profile, glycemic indices, adipocytokines, or obesity measures versus placebo, including across subgroup and sensitivity analyses.
waves.safety: Useful direct null evidence for NAFLD; it should not be generalized to diabetic neuropathy, where separate evidence exists.

waves.title: Hyaluronic acid and chondroitin sulphate instillation in chronic bladder diseases: a meta-analysis.
waves.population: patients with bladder pain syndrome, recurrent UTI, or post-radiation cystitis
waves.finding: Intravesical hyaluronic acid with or without chondroitin improved pain and urinary symptoms and reduced recurrent-UTI risk; randomized-trial subsets favored combined HA/ChS versus placebo or standard care.
waves.safety: This is intravesical treatment evidence, not evidence for oral chondroitin or hyaluronic-acid supplements.

waves.title: Impact of beetroot juice on oxidative stress in untrained individuals: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
waves.population: 360 non-athletic adults
waves.finding: Beetroot juice reduced pooled oxidative-damage biomarkers and increased total antioxidant capacity, with moderate-to-high heterogeneity across outcomes.
waves.safety: Redox biomarker improvements do not establish clinical disease benefit; dose, duration, and product standardization remain unresolved.

waves.focus: Meta-analysis of 9 RCTs in adults undergoing supratentorial craniotomy found perioperative magnesium sulfate reduced mean arterial pressure, fentanyl use, and S100B, while blood loss was not significantly changed; evidence is perioperative IV use, not oral supplementation.

Meta-analysis of 13 RCTs in diabetes/prediabetes found saffron/crocin reduced systolic blood pressure, fasting glucose, and AST, but not ALT, renal markers, or diastolic pressure; authors judged observed AST, SBP, and FBG effect sizes not clinically important.

Systematic review/meta-analysis of 17 studies found human-milk total choline rises from colostrum into transitional milk and then stabilizes in mature milk, with substantial variation by assay method, geography, and country income; this is compositional physiology rather than supplementation efficacy.

Meta-analysis of 13 randomized crossover studies found acute caffeine improved swimming performance by about 1.7% on average and increased post-exercise lactate; heterogeneity was substantial and apparent dose-response subgroup findings were exploratory rather than dosing guidance.

Individual-participant-data meta-analysis of 8 RCTs found prenatal balanced energy-protein supplementation reduced several small-vulnerable-newborn phenotypes, including preterm-SGA and term-SGA categories; control regimens and supplement composition varied across trials.

Biomarker-stratified meta-analysis of 7 pediatric ADHD RCTs found a small overall omega-3 effect, with larger estimated benefit in low-baseline omega-3 subgroups and no significant effect in normal/high or unstratified groups; evidence is preliminary and biomarker thresholds varied.

Systematic review/meta-analysis plus umbrella review found high-protein supplementation did not improve mortality or other major clinical outcomes versus conventional protein in critically ill patients; interventions lasting more than 14 days showed a slight mortality increase signal.

Umbrella review found modest pooled improvements in bone mineral density, muscle mass, and strength with probiotics/synbiotics, but heterogeneity was substantial, muscle findings were unstable in sensitivity analyses, and the authors concluded evidence does not support clinical recommendations.

Systematic review/meta-analysis found placebo-controlled capsaicin comparisons for orofacial pain did not reach statistical significance overall, while uncontrolled pre-post studies showed large pain reductions; adverse effects were more frequent but generally mild and local.

Systematic review/meta-analysis of zinc L-carnosine for oral mucosal injury found a severe-mucositis reduction under a common-effect model that was not significant under random effects; evidence certainty was low to very low across heterogeneous local formulations.

Meta-analysis of 81 observational studies found multiparous women were less likely than primiparous women to use folic acid before and around conception and early pregnancy, with high heterogeneity; this informs uptake behavior rather than folic-acid efficacy.

Systematic review/meta-analysis found vitamin D supplementation was associated with fewer seizures and higher vitamin D levels in drug-resistant epilepsy, but only four small studies contributed to the supplementation meta-analysis and larger trials are needed.

Meta-analysis of 49 RCTs reported higher remission measures, improved immune/hematologic markers, and fewer treatment-related toxicities when Chinese herbal medicine was added to conventional pediatric oncology care; 29 prescriptions and 136 substances make ingredient-level attribution impossible.

Bayesian network meta-analysis of 57 RCTs ranked several Chinese botanical decoctions favorably for migraine pain, frequency, or duration, but study-quality variation and indirect network comparisons limit confidence and prevent generalization to individual botanicals.

Systematic review/meta-analysis of 23 trials found melatonin was not clearly superior to placebo for chronic musculoskeletal pain in the main analysis, though some sensitivity and postoperative analyses favored melatonin; most effect estimates did not reach clinically important thresholds and certainty was low to moderate.

Meta-analysis of 25 RCTs found saffron modestly reduced fasting glucose, HbA1c, total cholesterol, and blood pressure in metabolic syndrome-related conditions, with no significant changes in insulin resistance, triglycerides, LDL-C, HDL-C, BMI, or waist circumference.

Meta-analysis of 9 prospective cohorts linked higher circulating choline/phosphatidylcholine with greater heart-failure incidence and higher betaine with adverse outcomes in established heart failure; these are observational biomarker associations, not evidence that choline supplementation causes harm.

Meta-analysis of 31 cohort studies found caffeine intake itself was not significantly associated with breast-cancer risk, while regular coffee showed a modest inverse association; the coffee signal should not be attributed to caffeine.

Twelve-week double-blind RCT in older adults with or at risk of sarcopenia found leucine-rich high-protein supplementation did not significantly improve body composition or physical performance, despite changes in selected gene-expression markers.

Systematic review/meta-analysis found omega-3 added to scaling and root planing produced small improvements in periodontal attachment and pocket depth, especially over longer follow-up, but heterogeneity was very high and evidence certainty was moderate to low.

Systematic review of 27 NAFLD studies found strong preclinical mechanistic signals but only 6 human studies; human findings suggested at most modest improvements in liver and metabolic markers, with insufficient evidence to establish alpha-lipoic acid as disease-modifying therapy.

Meta-analysis of adjunctive probiotic RCTs in schizophrenia found no significant benefit for negative symptoms, although inflammatory markers such as hs-CRP decreased; probiotics were generally well tolerated but symptom evidence remains very low certainty.

Three-level meta-analysis of 21 randomized crossover trials found acute capsaicin-analogue intake produced small improvements in overall athletic performance, particularly power and muscular endurance, but heterogeneity, publication bias, and very low certainty limit confidence.

Systematic review/meta-analysis found vitamin C supplementation significantly increased 24-hour urinary oxalate in both stone formers and non-stone formers, with no significant effect on urinary citrate or calcium; this supports a clinically relevant kidney-stone safety caution.

Meta-analysis found pregnancy nutrition education increased iron-folic-acid supplement adherence, raised hemoglobin, and reduced anemia risk; because the intervention was education rather than supplement efficacy itself, the finding belongs behind an intervention-context firewall.

waves.title: Melatonin in Preeclampsia: a Systematic Review of its Role in Pathogenesis and Therapeutic Potential.
waves.study: systematic review/meta-analysis; 9 included studies, only 1 human trial
waves.population: preeclampsia evidence base dominated by animal models
waves.finding: The only human trial reported a 6-day longer diagnosis-to-delivery interval with melatonin, while proteinuria increased; most favorable blood-pressure and oxidative-stress findings came from animal studies.
waves.safety: Human fetal safety and fetal benefit remain weak, conflicting, and insufficient for clinical recommendation.

waves.title: Impact of creatine supplementation on inflammation: evidence from a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized double-blind placebo trials.
waves.study: systematic review/meta-analysis of 8 randomized double-blind placebo trials
waves.population: healthy people, athletes, and clinical populations
waves.finding: Creatine did not significantly reduce acute or chronic CRP and did not significantly reduce chronic IL-6; isolated signals under intense endurance conditions were inconsistent.
waves.safety: Moderate-certainty evidence supports a null broad anti-inflammatory claim; protocols and populations varied.

waves.title: Local curcumin/turmeric-derived delivery adjunctive to scaling and root planing for periodontitis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
waves.study: systematic review/meta-analysis of 29 randomized or quasi-randomized clinical reports
waves.population: people with periodontitis receiving scaling and root planing
waves.finding: Local curcumin/turmeric adjuncts produced modest periodontal-pocket-depth reductions, but prediction intervals crossed the null and heterogeneity was high.
waves.safety: Low-certainty local-delivery evidence does not establish dose-response, formulation superiority, safety, or replacement of conventional antimicrobials.

waves.title: Time-dependent efficacy of zinc supplements in preventing oral mucositis after chemoradiotherapy: a meta-analysis.
waves.population: cancer patients receiving chemotherapy or radiotherapy
waves.finding: Zinc supplementation delayed oral-mucositis onset and reduced incidence and severe mucositis at several treatment time points, with benefits for pain and xerostomia.
waves.safety: Route- and dose-dependent subgroup findings are oncology-specific and should not be converted into general consumer dosing advice.

waves.title: Melatonin treatment for neonatal encephalopathy.
waves.study: Cochrane review of 4 randomized trials; 155 newborns
waves.population: term or late-preterm newborns with neonatal encephalopathy
waves.finding: Effects on mortality, neurodevelopmental disability, and MRI abnormalities remain very uncertain; the critical composite outcome was reported by only one small pilot study.
waves.safety: Very-low-certainty neonatal evidence is insufficient to establish benefit or safety.

waves.title: Omega-3 Fatty Acid Supplementation and Vascular Health Biomarkers - A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
waves.population: people with cardiovascular disease or vascular-risk conditions
waves.finding: Omega-3 supplementation did not significantly improve pulse-wave velocity, but improved augmentation index and flow-mediated dilation; effects differed by fatty-acid formulation.
waves.safety: Certainty ranged from moderate to low; dose-response estimates should not be treated as individualized dosing guidance.

waves.title: Efficacy and safety of Buyang Huanwu Decoction combined with α-lipoic acid for diabetic peripheral neuropathy: a systematic review with in-depth heterogeneity deconstruction and methodological appraisal.
waves.population: people with diabetic peripheral neuropathy
waves.finding: The herbal-decoction plus alpha-lipoic-acid combination improved response and symptom scores, while nerve-conduction results were extremely heterogeneous and HbA1c was not different.
waves.safety: Combination therapy prevents attribution to alpha-lipoic acid alone; adverse events did not differ, but methodological heterogeneity was substantial.

waves.title: Effects of Probiotic and Synbiotic Supplementation on Glycemic Indices in Adult Individuals with Prediabetes and Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Grade-Assessed Systematic Review and Dose-Response Meta-analysis of RCTs.
waves.population: adults with prediabetes or type 2 diabetes
waves.finding: Probiotic/synbiotic supplementation reduced fasting glucose, fasting insulin, HbA1c, and HOMA-IR on average.
waves.safety: Substantial heterogeneity and strain/product diversity prevent treating this as a uniform class effect or standardized regimen.

waves.title: Comparative effectiveness and safety of probiotics with psychotropic potential in mental health benefits in irritable bowel syndrome: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
waves.study: Bayesian network meta-analysis; 3,154 participants across 9 probiotic/placebo strategies
waves.population: people with irritable bowel syndrome
waves.finding: Some strains and probiotic combinations ranked better than placebo for quality of life, depression, or anxiety, but effects were strongly strain-specific and based partly on indirect network comparisons.
waves.safety: Network rankings should not be interpreted as proof of universal psychobiotic efficacy.

waves.title: Efficacy of probiotic supplementation for body weight management in overweight and obese adults: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials predominantly from East Asia.
waves.population: overweight and obese adults, predominantly East Asian cohorts
waves.finding: Probiotics produced small average reductions in body weight, BMI, waist circumference, and body-fat percentage, with no significant improvement in total cholesterol or triglycerides.
waves.safety: Effects were strain-, dose-, and context-specific; geographic concentration limits generalizability.

waves.title: Effectiveness of probiotic supplementation in managing depressive symptoms and inflammatory status in patients with depression: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
waves.study: systematic review of 13 studies; 7 included in meta-analysis
waves.population: people with depression
waves.finding: Probiotic supplementation was associated with improved depressive symptoms, but IL-6 and TNF-alpha were not significantly changed.
waves.safety: Clinical relevance and mechanisms remain uncertain; strain and formulation differences limit broad probiotic claims.

waves.title: The Complementary and Alternative Roles of Curcumin in Treatment of Ulcerative Colitis: An Umbrella Review.
waves.population: people with ulcerative colitis
waves.finding: Many pooled outcomes reached nominal statistical significance, but none were supported by high-certainty evidence.
waves.safety: Methodological shortcomings across source reviews leave curcumin's therapeutic effect uncertain despite favorable signals.

waves.title: N-acetylcysteine nano-spray versus conventional treatment in the management of radiotherapy-induced oral mucositis in oral cancer patients: a randomized clinical trial.
waves.population: oral cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy
waves.finding: A NAC nano-spray reduced mucositis severity and improved oral-health quality-of-life scores versus conventional therapy over six weeks.
waves.safety: Small sample and nano-spray delivery make this formulation-specific; it does not establish efficacy of oral NAC supplements.

waves.title: Correlations between iodine status and the risk of thyroid nodules, a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis.
waves.population: populations with varying urinary iodine status
waves.finding: Iodine status showed a U-shaped observational association with thyroid-nodule risk, with higher odds at deficiency and signals of increased risk at excess.
waves.safety: Cross-sectional evidence cannot establish that iodine supplementation causes or prevents nodules; residual confounding and heterogeneity remain.

waves.title: Effects of astaxanthin supplementation on human sperm quality during the freeze thaw process: a systematic review and meta analysis.
waves.study: systematic review/meta-analysis of astaxanthin use during sperm cryopreservation
waves.population: human sperm samples undergoing freeze-thaw processing
waves.finding: Astaxanthin improved progressive motility, viability, morphology, and selected kinematic parameters after thawing, but not total motility or DNA damage.
waves.safety: This is ex-vivo cryopreservation evidence, not evidence that oral astaxanthin improves male fertility.

waves.title: Vitamin D and Bisphosphonate Therapy for Optimizing Outcomes in Spinal Fusion: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
waves.study: systematic review/meta-analysis of randomized and prospective comparative trials
waves.population: patients undergoing spinal fusion
waves.finding: Vitamin D supplementation was associated with improved early fusion and modest functional outcomes versus placebo/no supplement, while bisphosphonates provided stronger fracture protection and similar one-year fusion.
waves.safety: Perioperative spine-surgery evidence is condition-specific and intertwined with active-drug comparator evidence.

waves.title: High versus standard dose folic acid supplementation for miscarriage prevention: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
waves.population: nonpregnant women of reproductive age trying to conceive
waves.finding: Higher-dose folic acid was associated with lower miscarriage risk among women who became pregnant and a higher pregnancy rate, but the intention-to-treat miscarriage analysis was not significant.
waves.safety: Evidence certainty was low to moderate; dose-comparison findings are insufficient for changing standard folic-acid dosing outside clinical guidance.

waves.title: Effects of the Edible Microalga Chlorella on Gut Microbiota and on Brain Health: Current Evidence and Emerging Links.
waves.study: systematic review with narrative synthesis; 21 included studies
waves.population: mixed evidence, predominantly animal models with limited human trials
waves.finding: Most included studies reported favorable gut-microbiota or neurobehavioral associations, but the evidence base was overwhelmingly preclinical and rarely measured gut and brain outcomes together.
waves.safety: Human efficacy remains unestablished; mechanistic/preclinical signals should not be promoted as clinical benefit.

waves.title: Zinc-based therapies for prevention and treatment of vulvovaginal candidiasis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
waves.study: systematic review of 11 studies including observational studies, 2 RCTs, and experimental studies
waves.population: women with vulvovaginal candidiasis
waves.finding: Lower systemic zinc was associated with VVC, but supplementation evidence was sparse: one RCT showed a nonsignificant reduction in reinfection and another reported improved pruritus with a zinc-containing adjunct.
waves.safety: Causality cannot be inferred from zinc-status associations, and current clinical trials are insufficient to support routine zinc therapy for VVC.

waves.title: Ginseng Bioactive Components as Gut-Brain Axis-Targeted Modulators: Therapeutic Potential and Mechanisms in Multifactorial Diseases.
waves.population: mixed disease models; evidence predominantly preclinical
waves.finding: Ginseng components show microbiome, barrier, inflammatory, and neurotransmitter effects across disease models, but the review explicitly notes that most evidence is preclinical.
waves.safety: Mechanistic plausibility does not establish clinical efficacy; human validation is still required.

waves.title: Enhanced Bioavailability of a Novel Oil-Based Lutein Formulation: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Single-Dose, Comparative Oral Bioavailability Study in Healthy Adults.
waves.study: randomized double-blind single-dose comparative bioavailability study; 80 healthy men
waves.population: healthy adults under fed conditions
waves.finding: A novel oil-based lutein formulation produced substantially higher Cmax and systemic exposure than a reference lutein formulation after one dose.
waves.safety: Both products were well tolerated, but this establishes formulation-dependent pharmacokinetics, not superior clinical efficacy.

waves.title: Efficacy and Safety of Salvia miltiorrhiza Extract (SAGX) Compared with Saw Palmetto in Men with Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms: A 12-Week, Randomized, Double-Blind, Parallel-Group Pilot Study.
waves.population: men with lower urinary tract symptoms
waves.finding: Salvia miltiorrhiza extract outperformed saw palmetto on several symptom and quality-of-life endpoints; the study does not establish saw palmetto efficacy versus placebo.
waves.safety: Small pilot and active-comparator design make this comparative evidence rather than a direct efficacy trial for saw palmetto.

waves.title: Effects of Probiotics on Markers of Oxidative/Nitrosative Stress and Damage Associated with Inflammation in Non-communicable Diseases: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Placebo-Controlled Trials.
waves.study: systematic review/meta-analysis of 15 studies/16 trials; 807 participants
waves.population: people with non-communicable diseases
waves.finding: Probiotics improved selected antioxidant/oxidative-stress markers, including total antioxidant capacity and malondialdehyde, while nitric oxide, 8-OHdG, IL-6, and TNF-alpha were not significantly changed.
waves.safety: Very high heterogeneity across several pooled markers and strain/population diversity limit class-wide claims.

waves.title: Omega-3 Fatty Acids Supplementation Improves Pulmonary Function and Clinical Outcomes in Critically Ill Patients: a Meta-Analysis.
waves.study: meta-analysis of 29 randomized trials; 2,551 critically ill patients
waves.population: critically ill adults receiving enteral or parenteral omega-3
waves.finding: Omega-3 interventions improved several oxygenation and inflammatory measures and were associated with shorter mechanical-ventilation duration and hospital stay.
waves.safety: Enteral and parenteral routes were pooled and the population is critically ill; findings cannot be generalized to ordinary oral omega-3 supplementation.

waves.title: Effects of probiotics on cognitive function across the human lifespan: a meta-analysis.
waves.population: participants across infancy, childhood, adulthood, and older age
waves.finding: Cognitive benefits varied by age and domain, with the strongest pooled signals in older adults for global cognition, processing speed, memory, and spatial ability; smaller domain-specific signals appeared in younger groups.
waves.safety: Age, strain, dose, and outcome heterogeneity prevent a universal probiotic-cognition claim; the review's apparent regimen optimum should not be treated as standardized dosing guidance.
